thread:
elaine: Heads up — the Dedicated canary in eu-west just showed a sustained p95 increase after the last runtime merge (~3x). Rolling back is blocking the rollout.

mike: saw that. p50 is fine, p95 and tail latency spikes and some 429s when concurrent connections hit ~1200.

sunita: errors look like queueing/backpressure in the request multiplexer, not obvious OOMs. attaching quick flame sample from the canary box:
```
# top samples
45% request_mux::enqueue
20% kvcache::lookup_miss
15% kernel_selector::choose_kernels
10% batcher::prepare_batch
5% nvtx::cuda_submit
```

kai: interesting that kernel_selector is showing up. could be fallback into slow kernels for certain sequence length bins. any recent changes around kernel scoring?

elaine: yeah, there was that PR that adjusted the sequence-length histogram weighting and heuristic thresholds (git sha: a1b2c3d). It landed in runtime/main about 6 hours before the canary.

mike: perf-ci also flagged a regression on the bench-suite ci/runtime/p95 test but it was marginal so it got a warning, not a blocker. perf-ci: @channel p95 +38% on runtime/main @ a1b2c3d.

perf-ci: automatically posting results — see CI run https://ci.redwood/98765 — p95 moved from 62ms -> 86ms on our synthetic 512-token workload.

sunita: I ran a short bisect across the last 10 merges. The one that flips the kernel scoring from LRU-prioritized -> score-prioritized is the culprit (CL 4579). Reproduces locally in a small repro harness.

elaine: can you paste the minimal repro? We need to know whether it's kernel selection logic or interacts with batching heuristics / KV cache.

sunita: minimal repro below (python harness):
```
# repro outline
client parallel 200
model sequence_length=512
send mixed small/big prompts
expect p95 < 100ms
```
It consistently p95 ~250ms with CL 4579, back to ~70ms when reverted.

kai: quick theory: the new scoring causes more kernel changes mid-sequence which busts the KV cache affinity -> more kvcache lookups and cache misses -> increased enqueue time for the mux. Matching that to the flame where kvcache::lookup_miss is 20%.

mike: also see queuing in batcher: enqueue latency distribution shifted right. Batcher stats from canary:
```
enqueue_latency_p95: 40ms -> 190ms
batch_size_avg: 6.1 -> 6.4
concurrent_inflight: up 2x
```

elaine: so batch size didn't change much, but enqueue latency did — consistent with mux/backpressure not batching decisions.

perf-ci: i ran `perf record` on the harness. Stack samples show heavy time in `kernel_selector::match_kernels` and `kvcache::rehash` on the regression commit.

sunita: I tried toggling the new heuristic flag off at runtime (`--kernel-score=legacy`) and the canary p95 dropped back. That confirms the scoring change.

elaine: can we safely revert CL 4579 in the release branch? Any downstream dependency?

kai: CL touches kernel scoring and a minor change in batching heuristics coupling. Revert should be isolated but will require a restart of the runtime processes. Risk is low compared to SLA exposure.

mike: customer-impact: two Dedicated tenants reported higher latencies (support tickets open). SLA risk flagged by SRE.

sre-oncall: filing incident P1 if rollout continues. We need the rollback or a hotfix within the hour.

elaine: ok plan: 1) revert CL 4579 from release candidate 2) redeploy canary to one host 3) run synthetic and production traffic overlay 4) if green, promote.

sunita: prepping revert PR now: https://git.redwood/revert/4582. I'll push test build and link CI.

perf-ci: CI check shows revert fixes the synthetic p95. Posting CI artifact: https://ci.redwood/98801.

deploy-bot: canary deployment started to group eu-west-1 (host id h-44f3) by elaine at 2026-03-18T12:22:00Z.

mike: monitoring — initial handshake looks ok. synthetic runner reporting p95 ~68ms. No 429s so far.

elaine: great. keep a close eye for 30m. If anything regresses we hold rollout.

kai: follow-up: we'll add an e2e perf test that mixes sequence lengths and parallelism to catch this variant in pre-merge CI. Also adding a KPI check that flags kernel churn (kernel-switches per request) > threshold.

sunita: noting root cause: aggressive kernel scoring change increased kernel switching and reduced KV affinity. Fix will be revert + follow-up PR that introduces score smoothing and a KV-affinity penalty.

mike: create a ticket for the follow-up and link to the revert PR. I'm opening ENG-1319.

elaine: thanks everyone — closing the blocker once canary is promoted. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: canary promoted to dc-eu group at 2026-03-18T12:49:00Z by elaine.

sre-oncall: marking incident as mitigated, will monitor for 4h then close.

sunita: follow-up work assigned to kai + sunita. I'll draft the design doc for score smoothing and KV affinity.

mike: also adding a perf regression test in the merge gate (p95 with mixed seqs) to prevent silent warnings becoming rollouts.

elaine: filing postmortem stub in incidents/ with notes and timeline.

mike: thanks — good catch by perf-ci and quick bisect by sunita.
